pages.text: Akaishi's "sealed-cavity matrices" in one line: $(4)wall off scattered machines into a hollow box and merge them into one big machine$(0).$(br2)$(bold)Universal rules:$(0)$(li)Casing is a $(bold)hollow sealed box with an odd edge length$(0) (3 or 5)$(li)Casings make the walls; ports and the controller sit on them, and the $(4)cavity must be empty$(0)$(li)Once formed it works as one unit — break any casing block and it instantly fails$(br2)Only two matrices have ever been built under these rules: one generates power, the other refines essence. Open their entries below for the exact layouts and stats.

$(bold)Generator Matrix (power):$(0) move the Energy Generator into a sealed cavity and burn fuel at a fixed multiplier. Two tiers — Basic 3×3×3 and Advanced 5×5×5; formed-structure stats and fuel/energy port hookups live in the $(l:akaishi:gen_matrix)Akaishi Generator Matrix$(/l) entry.$(br2)$(bold)Purifier Matrix (refining):$(0) a 3×3×3 cavity turned into a central refining line that crushes raw blocks and crystal blocks into essence in bulk at $(4)30x speed$(0). It runs on grid power and carries no fuel slot — see the $(l:akaishi:purifier_matrix)Purifier Matrix$(/l) entry.$(br2)Both are instances of the rules above: read this overview first, then dive into the entries and your layout will stay straight.

Single-block machines are where matrices start: the $(l:akaishi:generator)Energy Generator$(/l) and the $(l:akaishi:purifier)Akaishi Purifier$(/l) each have their own entry, and the two matrices grow out of them.
